Types of Sports Betting Markets Explained 2026

Compare sports betting markets such as match winner, totals and handicaps. Learn how each market is settled through the examples below.

If you’ve ever opened a betting app and felt overwhelmed by the number of options, winners, totals, handicaps, player bets, and dozens of strange abbreviations, you’re not alone. The world of sports betting markets can look complicated at first glance, but once you understand what each market represents, betting becomes less confusing and far more strategic.

In India, sports betting has grown rapidly, especially around cricket (IPL, international matches), football leagues, and even kabaddi. But here’s the truth: most players don’t lose because they “don’t know sports.” They lose because they choose the wrong market at the wrong time. A person may correctly predict a match winner but still lose money because the odds were poor or the market didn’t suit the match conditions.

That’s why learning the types of sports betting markets is crucial. Markets are not just “ways to bet.” They are different styles of risk, different ways of pricing probability, and different methods of finding value.

In this guide, we’ll break down:

  • The match winner market (simple but not always smartest)
  • over under betting (one of the most consistent markets)
  • handicap betting explained in a beginner-friendly way
  • prop bets in sports (player and event-based markets)
  • and why these are among the popular betting markets Indian bettors prefer in 2026

We’ll also include examples and practical tips, so this isn’t theory; it’s usable knowledge. Throughout the blog, you’ll also see how Lotus365 users can approach these markets more confidently.

LOTUS365 LOGIN

What Are Sports Betting Markets?

A “betting market” is simply a category of prediction. When you place a bet, you’re not just choosing a team; you’re choosing what kind of result you’re predicting.

So, instead of betting only on:

  • “Who will win?”

You can bet on:

  • “Will the total runs go above 180?”
  • “Will Team A win by 6+ runs?”
  • “Will Player X hit a fifty?”
  • “Will there be a wicket in the next over?”

Each of those is a different market.

This is why the same match can offer 50+ markets. Betting markets are created because fans don’t just enjoy results, they enjoy moments inside a match. Betting platforms like Lotus365 make these moments accessible by packaging them into markets.

If you want a broader beginner introduction before choosing markets, you can also read: The Complete Sports Betting Guide: How to Bet Smart and Win More (Even If You’re a Beginner)

Why Understanding Betting Markets Matters (Especially in India)

In India, many bettors enter sports betting through cricket, especially the IPL. Naturally, most people start with “team winner” bets because they feel simplest. But simplicity doesn’t always equal profitability.

Here’s the real advantage of understanding sports betting markets:

It helps you avoid low-value bets

Sometimes the favourite has odds so low that even if they win, the payout isn’t worth the risk. Learning different markets lets you find better pricing.

It helps you bet smarter in uneven matches

When a team is much stronger, “winner” odds may be tiny. Markets like totals and handicaps can offer more meaningful returns.

It helps you match the bet to the match

A slow pitch? Totals might be better.
A mismatch game? Handicap might be smarter.
Unpredictable weather? Some markets become risky.

In short, markets let you stop gambling and start thinking.

Match Winner Market (1X2 / Moneyline)

The match winner market is the most straightforward type of betting.

What it means

You bet on who wins the match.

Depending on the sport, it appears differently:

  • Cricket: Team A vs Team B (winner)
  • Football: 1X2 market
    • 1 = home win
    • X = draw
    • 2 = away win
  • Tennis: Player A vs Player B

Why it’s popular

It’s straightforward to understand, fast to choose, and feels intuitive.

Why it’s tricky

The match winner market often has two hidden problems:

  1. Low odds on favourites: The payout is small.
  2. Upset risk: One bad spell, injury, red card, or collapse changes everything.

Pro Tip (India bettors)

In cricket especially, the match winner market becomes more interesting live, because odds move with every over. If you want platform context, explore: LOTUS365

Over Under Betting (Totals Market)

If there is one market that consistently creates opportunities, it’s over-under betting.

What it means

You’re betting on whether the total will be:

  • above (Over) a fixed number
  • below (Under) a fixed number

This can apply to:

  • total match runs (cricket)
  • total goals (football)
  • total points (basketball)

Example (Cricket)

Total match runs line: 345.5

  • Over 345.5 = 346+ runs
  • Under 345.5 = 345 or below

Example (Football)

Total goals line: 2.5

  • Over 2.5 = 3 or more goals
  • Under 2.5 = 0, 1, or 2 goals

Why over/under is powerful

Unlike winner markets, you can bet totals even in “unpredictable winner” matches.

You’re not asking:
“Who will win?”

You’re asking:
“What kind of match will this be?”

That’s often easier to answer if you know the pitch, team style, weather, or lineups.

Best situations for over-under betting

  • Flat batting pitch → Over makes sense
  • Slow pitch / big ground → Under is valuable
  • Strong bowling attack early → Under
  • Dew + short boundaries → Over

Over/under is also one of the popular betting markets India bettors love because it feels less biased toward “big teams.”

Handicap Betting Explained (Spread / Run Handicap / Goal Handicap)

Now let’s get into the market most beginners avoid, and most smart bettors respect.

This is handicap betting explained properly.

What handicap means

A handicap is a “head start” or “disadvantage” given to a team to balance odds.

This market is useful when:

  • One team is much stronger
  • winner odds are too low to be useful

Cricket example (Run handicap)

Team A -15.5 runs
This means Team A must win by 16+ runs for your bet to win.

Team B +15.5 runs
Team B can:

  • win the match
    OR
  • lose by 15 runs or fewer
    and your bet still wins.

Football example (Goal handicap)

Team A -1.5 goals
Team A must win by 2+ goals.

Why handicaps are smart

Handicaps allow better odds and better pricing in mismatch games.

A match where a top team is likely to win becomes a more meaningful bet because you’re betting on how strongly they’ll win.

Best situations for handicap betting

  • Strong team with explosive finishers
  • One-sided squad matchups
  • When conditions favour the strong team (pitch/weather/venue)

If you’re betting on apps like Lotus365, handicaps are best when you already understand how a team performs under pressure.

Prop Bets in Sports (Specials & Player Markets)

Prop bets in sports are the most entertaining markets, and sometimes the most profitable if you follow stats.

What are prop bets?

Props are bets on events inside a game, not the final winner.

Examples:

  • player runs or goals
  • top scorer
  • number of boundaries/sixes
  • total corners (football)
  • wickets by a specific bowler

Cricket examples

  • “Player X to score 30+ runs”
  • “Total sixes in match over 14.5”
  • “Bowler Y to take 2+ wickets”

Why props are powerful

Because props reward specialisation.

You may not know who wins the match, but you may strongly know:

  • a batter’s form
  • a bowler’s matchup advantage
  • a team’s boundary rate
  • a football team’s corner pattern

In India, props have become more common because bettors want markets beyond the match winner.

Popular Betting Markets India Bettors Prefer (2026)

So, which markets dominate the Indian betting scene?

Here are the top popular betting markets India bettors typically focus on:

  1. Match winner market (especially in IPL & international cricket)
  2. Over under betting (team totals, match totals)
  3. Handicaps (especially for one-sided games)
  4. Prop bets (player performance)
  5. Live betting markets (next overruns, next wicket)

India’s betting behaviour has shifted toward live and props because people want control and faster outcomes.

How to Choose the Best Market for Your Betting Style

Not everyone should use every market. The smartest approach is choosing what suits your style.

If you’re a beginner

Start with:

  • match winner market
  • simple over under betting

Avoid:

  • too many props at once
  • complex multi-bets/parlays early

If you’re analytical

Use:

  • totals (over/under)
  • handicaps
  • player props based on stats

If you like live action

Focus on:

  • live winner
  • next overruns
  • next wicket
  • session betting (cricket)

What to Keep in Mind

Understanding sports betting markets is what separates random betting from smart betting. Once you know how the match winner market, over under betting, and handicap betting explained work, you can choose bets that suit the match situation instead of blindly following favourites. Add prop bets in sports for deeper strategy, especially if you track player form and match-ups. Common Questions & Answers

What are sports betting markets?

Sports betting markets are the different types of bets available on a sporting event. These sports betting markets include match winner bets, totals (over/under), handicap betting, and player prop bets. Understanding sports betting markets helps bettors choose options that match their knowledge and risk level.

What is the match winner market in sports betting markets?

The match winner market is one of the most popular sports betting markets. In this market, you simply bet on which team or player will win the match. In some sports like football, this sports betting market may appear as 1X2 (home win, draw, away win).

How does over-under betting work in sports betting markets?

Over-under betting is a totals-based option within sports betting markets. You place a bet on whether the total runs, goals, or points scored will be above or below a set number. Over-under sports betting markets are popular because they do not require predicting the match winner.

Can handicap betting be explained simply in sports betting markets?

In sports betting markets, handicap betting adds a virtual advantage or disadvantage to one side to balance the odds. For instance, a team may start at -15.5 runs or +1.5 goals. This type of sports betting market creates better value and more balanced betting options.

Are prop bets in sports betting markets good for beginners?

Prop bets are specialised sports betting markets based on player or event performance rather than the final result. While prop bets in sports betting markets can be profitable for informed bettors, beginners should start with simpler sports betting markets like match winner or over-under bets.

Game Setup

To play Teen Patti, gather 3-6 players around a table with a 52-card deck (no jokers) and chips or money for betting. Aces rank highest, followed by King, Queen, Jack, 10 down to 2. Before dealing, agree on the “boot” or ante—each player contributes an equal small amount (e.g., 1 chip) to start the central pot, ensuring everyone has skin in the game. Select a dealer randomly; they shuffle and deal three face-down cards to each player, one at a time, starting left of the dealer. The Blind vs. Seen Player Strategy: The Psychology of Teen Patti

One of Teen Patti’s most unique aspects is the Blind and Seen player dynamic. This mechanic creates entirely different strategies and psychological elements that don’t exist in games like poker.

A blind player bets without seeing their cards. They can only place a minimum bet. The advantage? Opponents can’t read your confidence level from your betting pattern since you don’t know your own hand strength. The disadvantage? You’re literally flying blind.​

A seen player has looked at their cards. They can bet higher amounts (at least double the blind bet). Your advantage now is knowledge—you know exactly what you’re holding and can make calculated decisions. Your disadvantage? Experienced opponents watch how you bet and can predict your hand strength.​

Here’s a real-world example: Imagine you’re playing with friends online. You get dealt your first three cards and choose to play blind. You place the minimum boot amount of ₹10. If you call at ₹40 without even knowing if you have good cards, you’re making a psychological bet—gambling on the possibility that you have better cards or that your Blind status might scare them off. This unpredictability is what makes blind play dangerous and powerful.

Professional players often use blind plays strategically at the start of sessions to build unpredictability. Then when they see cards and bet aggressively, opponents don’t know if they finally got good cards or are maintaining their unpredictable pattern.​

You’re sitting at a poker table with friends. Everyone knows how to play Texas Hold’em poker except you. Cards start flying. People are betting. Someone says, “Raise.” Another person says, “All in.” You’re completely lost, staring at your two cards, with no idea what’s happening around you, embarrassed to ask questions.

Here’s the good news: Texas Hold’em poker is actually incredibly simple once you understand the basics. Most people learn it in under 30 minutes. This guide shows you exactly how to play Texas Hold’em, the complete ranking of poker hands, the four betting rounds explained, the 5 beginner strategies that win, and answers to the 4 most common poker questions. What is Texas Hold’em Poker? Understanding the Game

Texas Hold’em poker is the most popular poker variant in the world. It’s played in casinos, home games, and online. Why? Because it’s simple, fast, exciting, and offers both luck and skill.

The basic concept:

  • Every player gets 2 private cards (only you see them)
  • 5 community cards appear face-up on the table (everyone shares them)
  • You make your best 5-card hand using any combination of your private cards and community cards
  • The player with the best hand wins the pot (all the money bet during the game)

Real-world example: It’s a Friday night poker game. You’re dealt Ace-King (strong hand). Three community cards come out: Ace, 5, and 7. You now have a pair of aces plus a king, which is a very strong hand. You see what cards are likely out there and decide to bet aggressively. Your friends fold. You win the pot without even going to the final cards. That’s the power of Texas Hold’em poker—you use strategy, not just luck.

The Complete Texas Hold’em Poker Hand Rankings (Strongest to Weakest)

To win at Texas Hold’em poker, you’ll need to understand hand rankings. Here they are, from strongest to weakest:

1. Royal Flush (Unbeatable)

  • Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10 all same suit
  • Example: A♠ K♠ Q♠ J♠ 10♠
  • Odds: 1 in 650,000 hands (rarest hand)
  • Beats: Everything

2. Straight Flush (Extremely Strong)

  • Five cards in sequence, all same suit
  • Example: 9♥ 8♥ 7♥ 6♥ 5♥
  • Odds: 1 in 72,000 hands
  • Beats: All hands except Royal Flush

3. Four of a Kind (Very Strong)

  • Four cards of same value plus any fifth card
  • Example: K♠ K♥ K♦ K♣ 7♠
  • Odds: 1 in 4,000 hands
  • Beats: Full House and lower

4. Full House (Very Strong)

  • Three of a kind and a pair
  • Example: Q♠ Q♥ Q♦ 5♣ 5♠
  • Odds: 1 in 700 hands
  • Beats: Flush and lower

5. Flush (Strong)

  • Five cards of the same suit (not in sequence)
  • Example: J♠ 9♠ 7♠ 5♠ 2♠
  • Odds: 1 in 500 hands
  • Beats: Straight and lower

6. Straight (Strong)

  • Five cards in sequence (any suits)
  • Example: 10♥ 9♦ 8♠ 7♣ 6♥
  • Odds: 1 in 250 hands
  • Beats: Three of a Kind and lower

7. Three of a Kind (Medium-Strong)

  • Three cards of same value and two different cards
  • Example: 8♠ 8♥ 8♦ K♣ 3♠
  • Odds: 1 in 47 hands
  • Beats: Two Pair and lower

8. Two Pair (Medium)

  • Two different pairs and one other card
  • Example: J♠ J♥ 5♦ 5♣ 2♠
  • Odds: 1 in 21 hands
  • Beats: One Pair and High Card

9. One Pair (Medium-Weak)

  • Two cards of same value plus three other cards
  • Example: 9♠ 9♥ K♦ 6♣ 2♠
  • Odds: 1 in 2.4 hands (most common winning hand)
  • Beats: High Card only

10. High Card (Weakest)

  • No matching cards, no sequence
  • Example: A♠ K♥ Q♦ J♣ 9♠ (Ace-high)
  • Odds: Very common
  • Beats: Nothing (loses to any pair)

How to Play Texas Hold’em Poker: Step-by-Step Process

Follow these steps and you’ll play your first hand correctly:

Step 1: Understand the Positions

Before any cards are dealt, understand the positions at the table:

  • Dealer Button (D): Moves clockwise each hand. This player acts last (advantage).
  • Small Blind: Left of the dealer. Must bet half the minimum.
  • Big Blind: Left of small blind. Must bet the full minimum.

Why positions matter: Players who act LATER have more information. This is a huge advantage.

Step 2: Receive Your Hole Cards

  • The dealer gives 2 face-down cards to each player
  • Only YOU see your cards
  • These are your private cards (hole cards)

Step 3: First Betting Round (Pre-Flop)

Starting with the player to the left of the big blind, each player can:

  • Fold: Discard your hand, lose any money bet
  • Call: Match the highest bet so far
  • Raise: Bet more than the previous bet
  • Check: Pass without betting (only if no bet yet)

Real example: You’re dealt King-Queen (strong). Blinds are $1/$2. You call the $2 bet. Two players fold. One player raises to $6. You call for $4 more (to match $6 total). Now $24 is in the pot.

Step 4: The Flop (First 3 Community Cards)

  • The dealer places 3 cards face-up on table (shared by all)
  • These are the community cards
  • Another betting round starts
  • Same options: Fold, Check, Call, Raise

Your hand gets MUCH stronger. You now see 5 cards (your 2 + 3 community cards).

Real example: You have King-Queen. The flop is King-7-2. You now have a PAIR of Kings. This is strong. You check (no bet yet). Another player bets $10. You call.

Step 5: The Turn (Fourth Community Card)

  • Dealer places 1 more card face-up (4th community card)
  • Another betting round
  • Your hand is now with 6 cards (your 2 + 4 community cards)

Step 6: The River (Fifth Community Card)

  • The dealer places final card face-up (5th community card)
  • Final betting round
  • Now you have ALL cards (your 2 + 5 community cards = 7 cards total)
  • You make your best 5-card hand from these 7 cards

Step 7: Showdown

  • Players still in the hand reveal their cards
  • The best 5-card hand wins the pot
  • The winner takes all money bet during the hand

5 Beginner Strategies That Win at Texas Hold’em Poker

Use these 5 strategies and you’ll beat most beginners:

Strategy #1: Play Fewer Hands, Play Them Aggressively

The Concept: Don’t play every hand. Only play strong hands. When you do play, be aggressive.

Strong Starting Hands:

  • Ace-Ace, King-King, Queen-Queen (best hands)
  • Ace-King, Ace-Queen (strong)
  • Pairs 8-8 and higher (playable)

Weak Hands to Fold Immediately:

  • 2-7, 3-8, 4-9 (don’t even play these)
  • Random low cards (5-2, 6-3, etc.)

Action: If you have a strong hand, BET BIG. If weak, FOLD.

Why it works: You’ll win most hands because you’re only playing when you have an advantage.

Strategy #2: Use Your Position (Act Last = You Win More)

The Concept: When you act after others, you have more information. Use it.

Position Strategy:

  • Button or Near Button: Play more hands, be aggressive
  • Middle Position: Play good hands only
  • Early Position: Only premium hands

Why it works: When you act last, you see what others do FIRST. That information is gold.

Real example: You’re on the button with 7-8 (normally the weak hand). Everyone folded to you. You can raise because you’re last, and likely everyone will fold. You win without seeing the flop.

Strategy #3: Know When to Fold

The Concept: Folding is a winning play. Your ego wants to “see the cards,” but that costs money.

Fold These Situations:

  • You have weak hand + someone bets big
  • You have medium hand and multiple opponents bet
  • You’re drawing for a card you need
  • You’re “chasing” money you already lost

Why it works: Saves your money for better hands. Pros fold 75% of hands dealt.

Strategy #4: Understand Pot Odds (Simple Version)

The Concept: Only call a bet if the pot gives you good odds.

Simple Rule:

  • If pot has $100 and bet is $10 (10 to 1 odds), call only if you have 10%+ chance to win
  • If pot has $50 and bet is $50 (1 to 1 odds), call only if there is a 50%+ chance to win

Why it works: Over time, you only make profitable bets.

Strategy #5: Bluff Rarely (Beginners Bluff Too Much)

The Concept: Pretend you have a strong hand when you don’t.

When to Bluff:

  • Only with strong hand ranges
  • Only against 1-2 opponents (not 4-5)
  • Only when board runs out cards
  • Only when betting makes sense

Why Beginners Lose: They bluff too much, get called, and lose money.

Winning Strategy: Play strong hands, fold weak hands. Let others bluff (and lose).

Common Texas Hold’em Poker Mistakes Beginners Make

Avoid these 5 mistakes and you’ll beat half the table:

Mistake #1: Playing Too Many Hands

  • You see Ace-2 and think, “Ace is strong.”
  • You play every hand because you’re impatient
  • Fix: Wait for strong hands. You’ll win more.

Mistake #2: Not Understanding Position

  • You play the same hands from every position
  • Fix: Play more hands from late position, fewer from early.

Mistake #3: Chasing Losses

  • You lost $50 last hand; now you’re betting huge
  • You’re trying to win it back immediately
  • Fix: Play your normal game. Don’t revenge bet.

Mistake #4: Over-Bluffing

  • You bluff almost every hand
  • Good players recognize this and call you down
  • Fix: Bluff less. Play strong hands and get value.

Mistake #5: Not Managing Your Bankroll

  • You bring your entire savings to the game
  • You go “all-in” on weak hands
  • Fix: Only bring money you can afford to lose. Play conservative amounts.

Common Questions & Answers

What’s the difference between Texas Hold’em and other poker games?

Texas Hold’em uses 2 private cards + 5 community cards. Other games (like Stud or Omaha) deal cards differently. Hold’em is simpler because you get 5 shared cards everyone can use. That’s why it’s the most popular variant in casinos and online.

Can I play Texas Hold’em poker online for real money?

Yes, online poker sites offer Texas Hold’em poker for real money. Choose licensed, reputable sites. Start small ($1-2 games) while you learn. Only play with money you can afford to lose.

How long does a typical Texas Hold’em poker hand take?

Usually 2-5 minutes per hand. Depends on how many players are left (fewer = faster), how many betting rounds go to the river (earlier folds = faster), and the table pace.

Is Texas Hold’em poker based on luck or skill?

Both, but skill dominates long-term. In the short term, luck plays a role. You might lose with the best hand due to bad luck. But over 1,000+ hands, skilled players beat unskilled players consistently. The best players make money year after year.
